# 09. Front-End Development

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Set engineering standards for durable static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with no backend and no proprietary lock-in.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A source structure for pages, partials or templates if used, assets, scripts, styles, generated files, and documentation.
- [ ] A dependency policy that prefers no dependency, then small open-source dependency, then build-time dependency over runtime dependency.
- [ ] A browser support policy based on the site's audience and analytics expectations.
- [ ] A JavaScript enhancement policy where essential content and navigation remain available without JavaScript unless impossible.
- [ ] A CSS standard covering custom properties, cascade, responsive units, container behavior, print styles, and reduced motion.
- [ ] An HTML standard requiring semantic landmarks, heading order, native controls, valid attributes, and accessible names.
- [ ] A code formatting and linting standard using free open-source tools when project complexity justifies them.
- [ ] A file size and dependency budget for CSS, JavaScript, fonts, images, and third-party code.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Pages must be valid, semantic, crawlable HTML before JavaScript enhancement.
- [ ] JavaScript must not be required for basic page reading, navigation, or contact information.
- [ ] All third-party code must have a documented purpose, owner, privacy review, performance cost, and removal path.
- [ ] CSS must be responsive by default and avoid fragile pixel-perfect assumptions.
- [ ] Assets must use relative or production-safe absolute paths that work on static hosting.
- [ ] Build outputs must be reproducible from source without paid services.
- [ ] The codebase must be understandable without proprietary editors or hidden builder state.
- [ ] Development choices must preserve accessibility, performance, security, and maintainability.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check HTML validation for duplicate IDs, missing required attributes, invalid nesting, and broken semantics.
- [ ] Check CSS for unused large blocks, hard-coded repeated values, fixed heights, overflow risks, and missing focus styles.
- [ ] Check JavaScript for global leaks, blocking work, unsafe DOM injection, unhandled errors, and inaccessible interactions.
- [ ] Check that local files do not include secrets, API keys, tokens, private URLs, or build credentials.
- [ ] Check that minified production assets are generated from readable source files where minification is used.
- [ ] Check that external links with target blank include noopener and noreferrer.
- [ ] Check that module scripts, defer, async, preloads, and font loading are used intentionally.
- [ ] Check that every dependency license permits the intended commercial use.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid adding frameworks for simple static interactions.
- [ ] Avoid inline event handlers, document.write, eval, unsafe innerHTML, and global click handlers without clear scope.
- [ ] Avoid layout built from divs when native landmarks and elements are available.
- [ ] Avoid CSS that depends on viewport width alone for text scaling.
- [ ] Avoid loading icon libraries, animation libraries, or utility frameworks for a tiny subset of features.
- [ ] Avoid code that only works from localhost or one hosting provider.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The production site must be small, readable, portable, and resilient.
- [ ] Every enhancement must degrade gracefully or fail silently without blocking the core page.
- [ ] The code must make future edits safer, not faster only for the first build.
- [ ] Static constraints must be treated as design inputs, not limitations to hide.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the Python audit script for HTML, links, assets, metadata, and common security issues.
- [ ] Add optional free tooling such as HTMLHint, Stylelint, ESLint, Prettier, Lighthouse CI, Pa11y, Axe, or Playwright when the project uses Node.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Development remains static HTML/CSS/JS with no custom backend, no database, no paid builder/plugin dependency, no proprietary template lock-in, and portable files.
- [ ] Project structure, file naming, semantic HTML, CSS organization, JavaScript purpose, shared components, header, footer, navigation, responsive layout, typography, images, icons, forms, CTAs, interactions, animation, accessibility, SEO, performance, analytics, consent, multilingual, blog, portfolio, product, integrations, legal, browser compatibility, errors, security, documentation, and QA are all checked.
- [ ] HTML has valid document structure, lang, title, metadata, one main landmark, one H1, logical headings, header/footer, semantic controls, no duplicate IDs, no placeholders, and accessible names.
- [ ] CSS has organized global/component/page layers, consistent tokens, readable selectors, no fragile overrides, responsive behavior, focus states, reduced motion, and no random one-off visual values.
- [ ] JavaScript enhances rather than replaces content, handles missing elements, avoids duplicate listeners, avoids globals where possible, has no console/debug/test code, no unsafe DOM patterns, and fails gracefully.
- [ ] Build-free and build-based workflows are both covered, with static output, minimal dependencies, documented commands, reproducibility, and no paid services.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
